[Leaf p441 / Page 439]

Priest: **"Let us attend!"** (*Во́ньмемъ*), and reads the 1st Gospel; and at the conclusion of the Reading, the Choir, instead of **"Glory to Thee, O Lord"** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀, Го́споди*), sings: **"Glory to Thy longsuffering, O Lord"** (*Сла́ва долготерпѣ́нїю Твоему̀, Го́споди*).[^591] The Priest, having kissed the beginning of the Reading, returns into the Sanctuary, and having closed the Holy Doors and bowed down toward the Holy Mysteries, departs to the sacristy, and having divested himself of the phelonion, goes to his place.
All these things take place also at the Readings of the other Gospels, except for the Little Ektenia and the censing, which according to the Typikon of our Triodia and the Typikon of the University of Lviv takes place only at the 1st Gospel, and at the 5 Sessional Hymns, and this only the censing of the Holy Table. For they say: "We do not sit at such Sessional Hymns, because the Priest censes the holy Altar, but standing we chant them."[^592] For the rest, we deem

---

[Leaf p442 / Page 440]

that one ought to cense not only at the Sessional Hymns, but also at all the other Gospels, for the censing is not for the sake of the Sessional Hymns, but for the sake of the Gospels, yet only around the Holy Table, as our Triodia have it, which mention censing only of the Holy Table; but it suffices to cense everything only twice, that is, at the 1st Gospel, and in the Canon at the Heirmos of the 4th Ode.
According to the Slavonic Typika, the 1st Gospel, and according to others also the 12th, is to be read by the Superior or Abbot. In the Cathedral Church the Hierarch reads them; while the other [Gospels are read by] the other sacred dignitaries according to the order of their dignity.[^593]
(The Deacons, if there be any, having vested from the beginning of Matins in violet dalmatics with the orarion, remain in the Sanctuary at their places until the Troparion **"When the glorious disciples"** (*Є҆гда̀ сла́внїи оу҆чени́цы*) begins to be sung for the third time; for then, having come with the Priest who is about to sing the Gospel, vested in a violet phelonion, before the steps of the Altar, and having bowed together with him toward the Holy Mysteries, they open the Holy Doors, cense all things according to custom, as at the beginning of the Liturgy, and return before the steps of the Altar; then, having handed over the censers and both bowed equally toward the Holy Mysteries, they go out each through his own door before the Royal Doors, and having bowed again toward the Holy Mysteries, they stand there until the second Deacon, after the chanting of the Troparion, recites the Little Ektenia; for then, having bowed toward the Holy Mysteries and changed their sides, they advance to the Analogion, so that, when the Priest has come to the Analogion, the first Deacon is at his right hand, and the second at his left. When the Priest has bowed toward the Holy Mysteries and come through the Holy Doors to the Analogion, the first Deacon proclaims: **"And that we may be accounted worthy..."** (*И҆ ѡ҆ є҆́же сподо́битися на́мъ*); Priest: **"Peace be to all"** (*Ми́ръ всѣ̑мъ*); second Deacon: **"Wisdom! Stand upright! Let us hear..."** (*Премꙋ́дрость, про́сти, оу҆слы́шимъ*); Priest: **"The Reading from N."** (*Ѿ и҆́мрекъ*); first Deacon: **"Let us attend!"** (*Во́ньмемъ*); Priest reads the Reading. When the Reading is finished, the Priest kisses the beginning of the Reading first himself, then the Deacon on the right, and after him also the one on the left, and all three return into the Sanctuary, the Priest through the middle doors, and the Deacons through the side doors; and standing together with the Priest before the

---

[Leaf p443 / Page 441]

steps of the Altar, they close the Holy Doors, and having all bowed equally toward the Holy Mysteries, they depart to their places. At the other Gospels, since the Little Ektenia is not said, the Deacons, having come before the Holy Doors, bow, and having changed their sides, go to the Analogion; and the Priest having taken his stand in their midst, they proclaim: **"And that we may be accounted worthy..."** (*И҆ ѡ҆ є҆́же сподо́битися*), and the rest, as above.
If it happens that a Hierarch or other sacred dignitaries are present, the Deacons ought to cense them before the Choirs, and neither the Priest nor the Deacons are to kiss the Gospel before the Hierarch and sacred dignitaries; and for this reason both Deacons carry the open Gospel together to them for kissing, then to the Priest standing in the Holy Doors; and when they have kissed it, they also kiss the same, and place it upon the Analogion; and having bowed deeply toward the Holy Mysteries, they return, each through his own door, into the Sanctuary.
5. After the chanting of the 1st Gospel there follow five Sessional Hymns, each of which has before it three Antiphons of Passion Troparia, and after itself one Passion Gospel. The number of Troparia is not equal in all the Antiphons, and according to the Typikon each is to be repeated,[^594] except for the Theotokion, with which each Antiphon is concluded, with the refrain **"Glory... Both now..."** (*Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ*).[^595]
6. The Beatitudes, with the Prokeimenon and the 6th Gospel at the end. The number of Stichera at the Beatitudes shall be 7, with **"Glory... Both now..."**, 8.[^596]
7. Psalm 50 and the 8th Gospel.
8. The Three-Ode Canon; Heirmoi twice, Troparia for 12, Katavasia after each Ode its Heirmos, both Choirs together. — After the 5th Ode, the Little Ektenia,

---

[Leaf p444 / Page 442]

and the Kontakion and Ikos; at the 9th Ode we do not sing **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*), but the Heirmos of the 9th Ode;[^597] after the 9th [Ode] we do not sing **"It is truly right"** (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), but the Katavasia;[^598] then the Little Ektenia, and the Exaposteilarion thrice with the refrain **"Glory... Both now..."**, according to custom; then the 9th Gospel.
9. At the Praises, Stichera for 4; **"Glory"**, one Sticheron; **"Both now"**, another; then the 10th Gospel.
10. **"To Thee glory is due"** (*Тебѣ̀ сла́ва подоба́етъ*),[^599] **"Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light"** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀ показа́вшему на́мъ свѣ́тъ*), and the Small Doxology.
11. The Ektenia **"Let us complete"** (*И҆спо́лнимъ*), and after the Exclamation **"For a God of mercy..."** (*Я҆́ко Бо́гъ ми́лости*)[^600] immediately the 11th Gospel.
12. The Aposticha; then the 12th Gospel.
13. **"It is good to give praise"** (*Бла́го є҆́сть*), Trisagion, **"Our Father"** (*Ѡ҆́тче на́шъ*), Troparion of Friday: **"Thou hast redeemed us"** (*И҆скꙋпи́лъ ны̀ є҆сѝ*).
14. The Ektenia **"Have mercy on us, O God"** (*Поми́луй на́съ, Бо́же*), and the Dismissal proper to Great Friday, the middle one, that is: Priest: **"Wisdom!"** (*Премꙋ́дрость*); Choir: **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*); Priest: **"Glory to Thee, O Christ..."** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀, Христѐ*), and the rest according to custom;[^601] but the 1st Hour we do not join.

### Erection of the Lord's Tomb
On Friday morning, before the beginning of the Royal Hours, there are placed upon the Holy Table the Plashchanytsia and the most beautiful Gospel, and there is erected before the Royal Doors the Tomb of Christ, beside which, according to the custom of the Northern

---

[Leaf p445 / Page 443]

and Western Latin Churches,[^602] the Holy Mysteries are exposed even until the Resurrection of Christ. And our Sluzhebnyks indeed command the Tabernacle (*Kivot*) with the Holy Mysteries to be placed upon such a Tomb; but the custom of our Cathedral Church is to expose the Holy Mysteries in the Monstrance (*Darookazalnytsia*) upon the High Altar, and to erect the Tomb of the Lord thus: above it there stands a Cross without the Crucified, with a shroud hung upon its crossbeam, and with the Instruments of Christ's Passion; it is adorned with costly cloth, and surrounded with many candlesticks and lamps, and vessels with small trees and flowers. The front board of the Sarcophagus is covered with crimson damask, to which is attached a white cloth, to which later the Plashchanytsia is to be pinned; the board itself is not flat, but inclined, so that the Plashchanytsia pinned to it may be visible and more accessible for kissing.

### Royal Hours
In the Cathedral Church they are sung at the 10th hour of the morning, together with the Typika (*Obidnytsia*) and with Vespers.[^603] We sing all things according to the Typikon of the Royal Hours of the Paramony of the Nativity of Christ, here on p. 181. However, since the Tomb is placed before the Royal Doors, the Analogion of the Gospel is placed a little below it, while the Analogion of the other Readings is placed still lower than this. And all things which at the Paramony of the Nativity

---

[Leaf p446 / Page 444]

the sacred ministers say before the Royal Doors, here they say before the Tomb; but they do not cense the Tomb, because until now there is nothing within it.

### Typika (Obidnytsia)
This we join to the 9th Hour; however, we do not say it from the beginning, as on the Paramony of the Nativity, but from the Beatitudes, without Stichera, and it shall be thus:
1. The Beatitudes... **"Glory... Both now..."**; **"Remember us, O Lord"** (*Помянѝ на́съ, Го́споди*) thrice.
2. **"The heavenly choir"** (*Ли́къ небе́сный*), with the Verses; **"Both now"**: The Creed (*Вѣ́рую*).
3. **"Pardon, remit"** (*Ѡ҆сла́би, ѡ҆ста́ви*), **"Our Father"** (*Ѡ҆́тче на́шъ*), the Kontakion of Great Friday.
4. **"Lord, have mercy"** (*Го́споди, поми́луй*) 12 times; **"All-holy Trinity"** (*Всесвята́я Тро́йце*) by the Priest.
5. **"Blessed be the Name of the Lord"** (*Бꙋ́ди и҆́мя Госпо́дне*) thrice; **"I will bless the Lord"** (*Благословлю̀ Го́спода*).
6. **"It is truly right"** (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*) with **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю херꙋві̑мъ*).
7. Priest: **"Glory to Thee, O Christ God"** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀, Христѐ Бо́же*), and the Dismissal of Great Friday, facing the people.
There is no Liturgy today under any circumstances, except for the Annunciation; but immediately after the Dismissal of the Typika we begin Vespers.

### On Great Friday Evening
#### At Vespers
*Note.*
1. At this Vespers there takes place an Entrance with the Gospel, and at its end, at the last Sticheron of the Aposticha, the Procession with the Plashchanytsia, and its deposition into the Tomb;[^604]

---

[Leaf p447 / Page 445]

2. All actions which the sacred ministers perform at ordinary Vespers before the Iconostasis, at this Vespers they perform before the Tomb of Christ.

#### Typikon
1. From the usual beginning even unto **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Го́споди, воззва́хъ*), all as at daily Vespers, without a Kathisma.
2. At **"Lord, I have cried"**, Stichera for 6; **"Glory"**, one Sticheron; **"Both now"**, another. — Entrance with the Gospel.
3. Instead of the Prokeimenon of the day there shall be the Prokeimenon of the Triodion, and the Paremia, and the second Paremia, and the third Paremia; then the third Prokeimenon, which is of the Apostle, and the Apostle, and Alleluia, and the Gospel. At the Alleluia censing takes place. **"Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!"** we say only at the 1st and 3rd Prokeimena; the Gospel we begin from **"Wisdom! Stand upright!"** Instead of **"Glory to Thee, O Lord"**, before the Gospel we say: **"Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord"** (*Сла́ва страсте́мъ Твои̑мъ, Го́споди*); and after the Gospel: **"Glory to Thy longsuffering, O Lord"** (*Сла́ва долготерпѣ́нїю Твоему̀, Го́споди*); likewise also at Matins.
4. **"Let us all say"** (*Рце́мъ всѝ*), **"Vouchsafe"** (*Сподо́би*), **"Let us complete"** (*И҆спо́лнимъ*), and the Aposticha.
5. At the last Sticheron of the Aposticha, that is at **"Thou Who clothest Thyself with light"** (*Тебѐ ѡ҆дѣ́ющагося свѣ́томъ*), there takes place the procession with the Plashchanytsia, and its deposition into the Tomb, according to the custom of our Cathedral Churches, thus: During the chanting of the Aposticha the Procession is arranged in the church; and the Monstrance (*Darookazalnytsia*) having been placed

---

[Leaf p448 / Page 446]

to the left on the Altar, the candles are lit on the Altar and on the Tomb, and the sacred ministers vest: the Hierarch and four most worthy Choir-clerics who are to carry the Plashchanytsia in all the sacred vestments of their Order, while the other Choir-clerics and Priests vest only in epitrachelia and phelonia, and others only in epitrachelia, and two Deacons in all the diaconal vestments. Burning candles are distributed to all the Choir-clerics and other Priests in the Sanctuary, and to the Brotherhood in the church; and the sacred ministers having approached the steps of the Altar and bowed deeply, the Hierarch ascends to the Altar, and having taken the Plashchanytsia spread out upon the Altar, hands it to four Choir-clerics, so that each holds one of its corners. Then the Deacon on the right ascends to the Altar, and having bowed deeply, brings out the Tabernacle (*Kivot*) with the Holy Mysteries, and having placed it upon the (folded) Iliton, takes out from it the Lamb with the pyx (*kletka*) in which It rests, not touching It with fingers, but holding by the pyx, and places It into the Monstrance (*Darookazalnytsia*), having securely closed it; and having closed the Tabernacle, he places it into the Tabernacle-shrine (*Skynia*), and having bowed and closed it, and having placed the Monstrance in the midst of the Iliton facing the people, he steps back a little to the side, until the Hierarch, kneeling, censes the Holy Mysteries thrice, each time with a bow at the end, and having taken upon himself the small omophorion (*omophorets*), approaches the Holy Table; for then the Deacon, having bowed down before the Holy Mysteries and taken Them with both hands, delivers Them to the Hierarch, who has first made a metania, who turns by the right toward the people; and the Singers beginning to sing **"Thou Who clothest Thyself"** (*Тебѐ ѡ҆дѣ́ющагося*), he goes out behind the Clergy from the Royal Doors by the north side of the Tomb into the church; and having entered under the Baldachin, surrounded by candle-bearers, with the two Deacons preceding and censing unceasingly, he advances behind all to the Doors of the church,

---

[Leaf p449 / Page 447]

the Cross-bearer going before all, then the Banner-bearers, then four maidens bearing icons, then the Church Brotherhood, the students of the Seminary, the Choir of singers of the Seminary, then from the Royal Doors the Priests, the Choir-clerics, the four sacred dignitaries carrying the Plashchanytsia facing with its feet toward the people; and at the end the Hierarch with the Deacons censing, and the candle-bearers. As the procession exits from the church, it turns to the right, that is to its northern side, and having circled it thrice (or as they do there today, once), returns into the church; and those with the Plashchanytsia and the other Priests having halted before the Tomb, the Hierarch with the Deacons returns by the south side of the Tomb, through the Royal Doors, into the Sanctuary; and the Deacon on the right having received from his hands the Holy Mysteries and placed Them upon the Holy Table, the Hierarch, having bent his knees and laid aside the Omophorion (Velum), censes Them thrice with the bowing of his head; and the Deacon, having bowed, exposes Them above the Tabernacle-shrine (*Skynia*); then all three having bowed before the steps of the Altar, they go out, the Hierarch through the middle doors, and the Deacons through the side doors, before the Tomb; and the Hierarch, having received the Plashchanytsia from the Choir-clerics holding it, lays it upon the Tomb, and they pin it down to the Tomb; and when the Singers finish **"Now lettest Thou depart"** (*Ны́нѣ ѿпꙋща́еши*), and the Trisagion and the rest with **"Our Father"** (*Ѡ҆́тче на́шъ*), the Hierarch exclaims: **"For Thine is the Kingdom"** (*Я҆́ко Твоѐ є҆́сть Ца́рство*), and beginning, sings with the concelebrants the Troparion **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный Іѡ́сифъ*), and at the end makes with the concelebrants a deep metania, while all the people make a great prostration to the ground; then for the second time the same Troparion the second Choir [sings], and all make a metania and prostration as before. And where there is only one Choir, then the first time this Troparion is sung by the sacred ministers, the second time by the Choir, the third time half by the sacred ministers, and the remainder from the Plashchanytsia and below

---

[Leaf p450 / Page 448]

by the Choir.[^605] And after the chanting of the Troparion and after the prostrations they kiss the Plashchanytsia, all according to rank, having made before the kissing a single metania, first the Hierarch, then the other sacred ministers according to the order of their dignity; and there takes place the Great Dismissal proper to this Saturday, after which the sacred ministers return into the Sanctuary, and having left the Royal Doors open even until the end of Bright Week, divest themselves of the sacred vestments, and go each to his own home; while the people follow to kiss the Plashchanytsia.[^606]

---

[Leaf p451 / Page 449]

*Note.*
1. Where there is only one Priest, let him choose for himself four most honorable lay men for the carrying of the Plashchanytsia.
2. The Pastor of souls, even if he has several churches, in the mother church sings Vespers with the carrying out of the Plashchanytsia, but in filial churches only carries out the Plashchanytsia, thus: after **"Blessed is our God"** (*Благослове́нъ Бо́гъ на́шъ*) and **"Come, let us worship"** (*Прїиди́те, поклони́мся*) thrice, immediately the Procession with **"Thou Who clothest Thyself"** (*Тебѐ ѡ҆дѣ́ющагося*), and after the Procession: **"Glory to Thee, O Christ God"** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀, Христѐ Бо́же*), and the Dismissal, and **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный Іѡ́сифъ*) thrice, with prostrations.

### Little Compline
This, as also the Midnight Office, we read in private.
At Compline the Canon of the Crucifixion of the Lord, and of the Lament of the Most Holy Theotokos.
After **"It is truly right"**, the Kontakion of Great Saturday.

### Saturday Midnight Office
All according to custom.

### Matins of Great Saturday
*Note.*
1. This we sing usually on Friday evening after sunset, although the Typika appoint it in the 7th hour of the night.
2. The sacred ministers remain throughout the whole Matins before the Lord's Tomb, where seats are placed for them, and a table with

---

[Leaf p452 / Page 450]

candlesticks and Books, so that sitting they may sing from there the Order, the Priests in epitrachelia and phelonia, and the Deacons in dalmatics, of violet color.

#### Typikon
1. From **"Blessed is our God"** (*Благослове́нъ Бо́гъ на́шъ*) even unto **"Come, let us worship"** (*Прїиди́те, поклони́мся*) exclusively, all as usually at Matins; then after the 12 **"Lord, have mercy"**, having omitted **"Come, let us worship"**, immediately the Priest: **"Glory to the holy..."** (*Сла́ва святѣ́й*), and the rest with the Six Psalms even unto **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*), as usually.[^607]
2. At **"The Lord is God"**, Troparion: **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный Іѡ́сифъ*) twice. **"Glory"**: **"When Thou didst descend unto death"** (*Є҆гда̀ снизше́лъ є҆сѝ къ сме́рти*); **"Both now"**: **"Unto the Myrrh-bearing Women"** (*Мѵроно́сицамъ жена́мъ*).[^608]
3. Kathisma 17 (The Blameless / *Neporochni*) in three Stases, with the Funeral Troparia, with censing at the beginning of each Stasis, and the Little Ektenia after each Stasis.
Concerning the censing we deem that it will suffice to cense only the Plashchanytsia (together with the Holy Mysteries, if anywhere They are placed upon the tomb) and the Choirs and people.[^609]
Concerning the Funeral Troparia, called in the Greek Triodia *Ἐγκώμια* (Praises / *Pokhvaly*), be it known that before each of them is chanted one verse of the Kathisma, until all are completed; only the 1st Troparion of each Stasis (and in the editions of our Pochaiv Triodia also the 2nd Troparion of the 2nd Stasis)

---

[Leaf p453 / Page 451]

is sung without a Verse, and this both at the beginning and at the end of the Stasis, except for the 3rd Stasis, after which the 1st Troparion is not sung, nor is the Little Ektenia said, but immediately **"The Angelic Host"** (*А҆́нгельскїй собо́ръ*), and after its chanting the Little Ektenia.
4. After **"The Angelic Host"** with the Little Ektenia: Sessional Hymn, and Psalm 50, and the Canon.
5. The Canon: Heirmoi twice, Troparia for 12. We say the refrain: **"Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thy holy burial"** (*Сла́ва Го́споди, святѡ́му погребе́нїю Твоему̀*). Katavasia: the Heirmos of the Canon, both Choirs together.
After the 3rd Ode, the Sessional Hymn; after the 6th, the Kontakion and Ikos; at the 9th Ode we do not sing **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*),[^610] and after the 9th [Ode] we do not say **"It is truly right"** (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), but the Heirmos; and afterwards instead of the Exaposteilarion we sing **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (*Свѧ́тъ Госпо́дь Бо́гъ на́шъ*) thrice.
6. At the Praises, 4 Stichera; then one at **"Glory"**, and one at **"Both now"**.
7. At the Great Doxology we make the Entrance with the Gospel, and instead of the single Troparion which is after the Doxology, there shall be one Funeral Sticheron, and two Troparia, and three Readings, that is: one of Prophecy, one of the Apostle, and one of the Gospel.
And the Entrance takes place thus: During the chanting of the Stichera of the Praises, the Priest and Deacons, if there be any, having bowed deeply before the Plashchanytsia, together with the Holy Mysteries, go to the vestry and vest in all the sacred vestments of their Order. While the Doxastikon (*Naslavnyk*) is being sung, likewise the other sacred ministers who are before the Lord's Tomb, vested in phelonia, having bowed together deeply, depart into the Sanctuary;

---

[Leaf p454 / Page 452]

and the Priest with the Deacons having come before the steps of the Altar, they also stand together with him on this side and that; and all having bowed down toward the Holy Mysteries, the Priest proclaims after the chanting of the Stichera of the Praises: **"Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light"** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀ показа́вшему на́мъ свѣ́тъ*); then, having placed incense for the Deacon on the left, as the Doxology is ending he ascends to the Altar, and having taken the Gospel from the Holy Table, hands it to the Deacon on the right, and they make the Entrance in all things as takes place at the Liturgy, preceded by the candle-bearers, and the Deacon with the censer; and they halt before the Lord's Tomb, the Deacon on the right at the right hand, and the one on the left at the left hand of the Priest, closer to the Tomb, while the other sacred ministers are on two wings, a little lower, with the Priest, awaiting the end of the Trisagion and the Sticheron **"Come, let us bless Joseph"** (*Прїиди́те, оу҆блажи́мъ Іѡ́сифа*). When this has taken place, the first Deacon, raising his orarion toward the people, proclaims: **"Let us attend!"** (*Во́ньмемъ*); the Priest, signing the people: **"Peace be to all"** (*Ми́ръ всѣ̑мъ*); the second Deacon, raising his orarion: **"Wisdom, let us attend!"** (*Премꙋ́дрость, во́ньмемъ*); and we sing the Troparion **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный Іѡ́сифъ*) once. The Deacon having placed the Gospel upon the Analogion facing the people, and the other having handed over the censer, we sing also the Troparion of the Prophecy once.[^611]

---

[Leaf p455 / Page 453]

Then again: **"Let us attend! Peace be to all! Wisdom, let us attend!"**, and the Prokeimenon, and the Reading of the Prophecy, and the other Prokeimenon, and the Reading of the Apostle, and Alleluia, at which the Deacons cense the Tomb, the presiding sacred ministers, and the people. After these, the first Deacon: **"Wis-**

---

[Leaf p456 / Page 454]

**-dom! Stand upright! Let us hear..."**; Priest: **"The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew"**; Choir: **"Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord"** (*Сла́ва страсте́мъ Твои̑мъ, Го́споди*); the second Deacon: **"Let us attend!"**; and the Priest sings the Gospel facing the people; and at its conclusion, the Choir: **"Glory to Thy longsuffering, O Lord"** (*Сла́ва долготерпѣ́нїю Твоему̀, Го́споди*). Then the Priest, having kissed and closed the Gospel, leaves it upon the Analogion; and the first Deacon says the Ektenia **"Let us all say"** (*Рце́мъ всѝ*), and the second **"Let us complete"** (*И҆спо́лнимъ*), all according to custom.
8. [9 in original] After the Dismissal, having chanted the Troparion **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный Іѡ́сифъ*) thrice with prostrations, as at Vespers, and the Deacon having taken the Gospel from the Analogion, the sacred ministers depart into the Sanctuary and divest themselves of their vestments; and the Deacon having placed the Gospel upon the Holy Table and bowed, departs and divests himself.

#### At the Hours
1. At all [Hours], the Troparion and Kontakion of Great Saturday.
2. The Dismissal of Matins of Great Saturday.

#### At the Typika (Obidnytsia)
As on Great Thursday, here on p. 435; however, the Greek Triodion does not appoint the Typika.

### On Great Saturday Evening
#### At Vespers with the Liturgy of Basil
1. According to the custom of the Cathedral Church, this Vespers begins at the 9th hour of the day.[^612]
2. The Vespers of this day is only one, and that great, with the Liturgy of Basil, and an All-Night Vigil shall not

---

[Leaf p457 / Page 455]

take place; but after the Ambo Prayer, or (as the Typika have it) after the Dismissal of the Liturgy, there shall be the blessing of loaves, as usually at a Vigil.
3. The form and Typikon of this Vespers is the same as that of the Vespers with the Liturgy celebrated on the Paramony of the Nativity of Christ, here on p. 189, without **"Blessed is the man"** (*Блаже́нъ мꙋ́жъ*); only here after **"O Joyful Light"** (*Свѣ́те ти́хїй*) there shall be no Prokeimenon, but immediately the Readings, 15 in number, and between the Readings there shall be no Troparia; but at the 6th Reading all the Verses of the Canticle of Moses are read with the refrain: **"For gloriously is He glorified"** (*Сла́вно бо просла́вися*); and at the 15th Reading the Verses of the Canticle of the Three Youths are read with the refrain: **"Praise the Lord and exalt Him above all forever"** (*Го́спода по́йте, и҆ превозноси́те є҆го̀ во вѣ́ки*); and instead of Alleluia we sing the last verse of Psalm 81 with the other Verses thereof, in the manner of a Prokeimenon.[^613] Dismissal of Saturday Matins.
4. Although the Service of a Feast usually begins with the Vespers of the preceding day, and for this reason the entire Resurrection Service ought to be with bright sacred vestments, nevertheless, because the Liturgy with which Vespers is sung is still of Saturday, for this reason a portion of the Stichera sung at **"Lord, I have cried"** is concerning the descent of the Saviour's soul into Hades; and for this reason from the beginning of this Vespers we take violet vestments, but later we change them and take bright ones after the reading of the Apostle, at the verses replacing the Alleluia, so that we may read the Gospel already in bright vestments.[^614]

---

[Leaf p458 / Page 456]

5. Throughout all of Bright Week, beginning from the Vespers of this day, the Resurrection Service is sung, and besides the Stichera of the Triodion there are sung also the Resurrection Stichera of the Octoechos, of a different Tone daily, that is: on Sunday, Tone 1; on Monday, Tone 2; on Tuesday, Tone 3; on Wednesday, Tone 4; on Thursday, Tone 5; on Friday, Tone 6; on Saturday, Tone 8, having skipped Tone 7.

#### At Compline
In Greek and Slavonic Triodia, except our own, Compline is not appointed; but from the Blessing of Loaves even unto the Funeral Order sung immediately before Paschal Matins, there is appointed the reading of the entire Book of the Acts of the Apostles, although among us today scarcely in Cathedral and Seminary Churches are these Acts sung; they are sung to verses by clerics alternating two by two.
This Compline would have to be small. For the rest, even our Triodion itself leaves to discretion whether to read it or not; for it says concerning it: "if it be." In that case, there is appointed in our Triodion the Canon of the Burial of Christ, and of the Lament of the Most Holy Theotokos. After the 9th Ode, instead of **"It is truly right"**, the Heirmos of this Ode; and after the Trisagion, the Kontakion of Great Saturday.

### Office in Place of the Midnight Office (Paschal Nocturns)[^615]
*Note.* This we sing before the Plashchanytsia immediately before Paschal Matins, either only in epitrachelion and phelonion, as usually in the provinces, or in all the sacred vestments, of violet color, as in Cathedral Churches.

---

[Leaf p459 / Page 457]

#### Typikon
1. From the usual beginning even unto **"Come, let us worship"** (*Прїиди́те, поклони́мся*), we say all things as usually at the Midnight Office; and immediately Psalm 50 and the Canon.
2. The Funeral Canon of Great Saturday Matins: **"The wave of the sea"** (*Волно́ю морско́ю*); according to the Typikon, the Heirmoi twice, and the Troparia for 12 (today with the Heirmos for 4), with the refrain: **"Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thy holy burial"** (*Сла́ва Го́споди, святѡ́му погребе́нїю Твоему̀*); and at the end the Katavasia, the Heirmos, both Choirs together.
After the 3rd Ode, the Sessional Hymn; and after the 6th, the Kontakion and Ikos of Great Saturday; after the 9th [Ode] there is no **"It is truly right"**, but the Heirmos of this Ode.
3. Trisagion, and the rest with **"Our Father"** (*Ѡ҆́тче на́шъ*), and the Troparion **"When Thou didst descend unto death"** (*Є҆гда̀ снизше́лъ є҆сѝ къ сме́рти*).
4. The Ektenia **"Have mercy on us, O God"** (*Поми́луй на́съ, Бо́же*), which is at the Midnight Office, and the Dismissal of Great Saturday Matins,[^616] beginning from **"Glory to Thee, O Christ God"** (*Сла́ва Тебѣ̀, Христѐ Бо́же*).
5. [4 in original] Then toward the end: **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный Іѡ́сифъ*) thrice with prostrations, as after Great Saturday Matins; however, the Plashchanytsia is kissed only by the sacred ministers, according to rank; and the Hierarch, having taken the Plashchanytsia from the Tomb, delivers it to four Choir-clerics, and thus all the sacred ministers return into the Sanctuary; and four Choir-clerics having hung the Plashchanytsia behind the Holy Table above the High Place,[^617] they go to the vestry, and having divested themselves of the violet vestments, vest in all the bright sacred vestments of their Order; and at that time all the candles in the church are lit.

---

[Leaf p460 / Page 458]

*Note Concerning the Plashchanytsia.*
Concerning the time and place of the deposition of the Plashchanytsia we find no ancient Typikon; for this rite is later, and varies according to different regions. According to the custom of our First-Cathedral Church, the Plashchanytsia remains hung behind the Holy Table above the High Place from Paschal Matins even unto the Apodosis of Pascha inclusively, that is until the Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of other churches of ours, the Plashchanytsia, having been taken from the Tomb before Paschal Matins, is placed upon the Holy Table, where it lies throughout all of Bright Week, and from Thomas Sunday even unto the Apodosis of Pascha, behind the Holy Table. According to others, it lies upon the Holy Table from Pascha until its Apodosis.[^618] When therefore the Plashchanytsia lies upon the Holy Table, the Iliton with the Gospel is placed upon it, and the Liturgy is celebrated upon it. However, it is better to keep the Plashchanytsia behind the Holy Table, because lying upon the Holy Table it is not a little damaged by candles dripping upon it.

## Beginning of the Holy Pentecostarion

### Procession with the Holy Mysteries Around the Church
After the taking of the Plashchanytsia from the Tomb and carrying it into the Sanctuary, the sacred ministers, having vested in all the brightest sacred vestments of their Order, go out before the steps of the Altar, and having all bowed equally and deeply toward the Holy Mysteries, bend their knees, and take lighted candles; likewise also the Brotherhood in the church. The Deacon on the right (or the Priest himself, if there be no Deacons), having approached the middle of the Holy Table and bowed deeply, sets aside the Gospel on the right side thereof, and having taken

<!-- END COHORT 1899_dolnytsky_typikon_cohort23 -->

---

<!-- START COHORT 1899_dolnytsky_typikon_cohort24 -->

[Leaf p461 / Page 459]

the Holy Mysteries from the top of the Tabernacle (*Skynia*), and having placed them upon the Iliton, steps back a little to the side; and the Hierarch (or presiding Priest), having censed the Holy Mysteries thrice according to custom, and put on the Omophorion, standing up and ascending the steps, and having bowed down, receives the Holy Mysteries from the hands of the Deacon, turns toward the people, and when he begins to sing the Sticheron **"Jesus is risen from the tomb"** (*Воскре́съ І҆исꙋ́съ ѿ гро́ба*), while all the bells chime joyfully, the Procession around the church takes place, in all respects as was depicted on Great Friday at Vespers, here on page 445, except for the Plashchanytsia, which here, by order of Cardinal Sembratovych of blessed memory, is not to be carried, because it does not agree with the joy of the Resurrection; rather, it is fitting to carry the Icon of the Resurrection, as the Triodion has it at the beginning of Paschal Matins during the Procession to the church doors. And when the Superior begins to sing the Sticheron **"Jesus is risen from the tomb"**, the Choirs and the people follow in singing the same, and they sing it, repeating it until the Procession is completed, that is, a threefold, or at least a single circuit around the church, which when it is completed, all enter into the church, while the banner-bearers and icon-bearers remain before the church doors to avoid commotion during the second Procession; while in the church the cross-bearer with two candle-bearers, the Brotherhood, the Choirs, and the Clergy arrange themselves for the Procession; and when the sacred ministers have entered into the Sanctuary, the Superior ascends the Altar, and having turned toward the people, blesses them with the Holy Mysteries, saying in a gentle voice: **"Save, O God, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance"** (*Спасѝ, Бо́же, лю́ди Твоя̀, и҆ благословѝ достоя́нїе Твоѐ*); and having set down the Holy Mysteries upon the Altar, he descends before the steps, bends his knees, and having laid aside the Omophorion, censes the Holy Mysteries thrice according to custom; and the Deacon, having approached the Holy Mysteries and bowed deeply, removes them with the lunette from the Monstrance (*Darookazalnytsia*), and places them into the Tabernacle (*Kivot*),

---

[Leaf p462 / Page 460]

and the Tabernacle (*Kivot*) into the Ark (*Skynia*), and having bowed down, closes it. And where there is no Monstrance (*Darookazalnytsia*), the Holy Mysteries are exposed with the Tabernacle (*Kivot*), and with it are closed in the Ark (*Skynia*).

*Note.* This Procession with the Holy Mysteries before Paschal Matins is a later adornment of our Churches, borrowed neither from the Greeks nor from the Romans, but from the Latin Churches of these regions, and an added magnificence to our Paschal Matins; nor is it set down in our Typika.

## Paschal Matins

1. **Procession Before the Church Doors.** As all the people go out from the church, the sacred ministers likewise go out after them, and the Procession takes place thus: when the sacred ministers have taken their stand, in all their bright sacred vestments, before the steps of the Holy Table, the Superior takes the Cross, and the Deacon the Censer; and when all have bowed equally and deeply toward the Holy Mysteries and turned toward the west, the Superior begins to sing the Sticheron **"Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior"** (*Воскресе́нїе Твоѐ, Христѐ Спа́се*); and while all follow in singing the same, they go out from the Sanctuary, the Priests indeed through the Royal Doors, and the other sacred ministers through the Deacon's Doors into the church, and while all the bells are ringing, they go even unto the great Church Doors; and having gone outside the church, they stand orderly, facing the church doors, which are immediately closed.[^619] And inside the church there are placed upon the

---

[Leaf p463 / Page 461]

Holy Table, first of all the Icon of the Resurrection of Christ, usually upon the Artos, and other venerable Icons, and Reliquaries, and the most precious Gospels, or whatever else of sacred things, all these according to the number of Priests who intend to give them to the people to kiss at the end of Matins; while outside before the church doors the beginning of Matins takes place thus.[^620]

2. **Beginning of Matins.** Immediately upon the closing of the church doors, the presiding Priest, holding in his left hand the Cross, and in his right the Censer, and censing the church doors,[^621] proclaims with a loud voice: **"Glory to the holy..."** (*Сла́ва ст҃ѣ́й*), and the rest.

---

[Leaf p464 / Page 462]

and when the Choirs have answered: **"Amen"**, having handed over the Censer, he sings with a loud voice the Troparion **"Christ is risen"**, then all sing the same; and a second time the Priest sings the same, and all the same; and a third time the Priest sings the same, and all the same; then the Priest in a clear voice proclaims the Verses, while all after each verse chant the same Troparion once.[^622] Finally the Priest, having sung in a higher voice the same Troparion only up to **"trampling down death by death"** inclusively, opens the doors, while all conclude: **"and upon those in the tombs bestowing life"**; and while all the bells are rung again, all enter into the church.[^623] But the Morning Prayers at

---

[Leaf p465 / Page 463]

Paschal Matins throughout all of Bright Week are not said, because these are linked to the Six Psalms, and since the latter here give way, the Prayers also give way. If the Prayers were to be said, the Typikon would have had to indicate where to say them, for during the Verses **"Let God arise"**, which occupy the place of the Six Psalms, they cannot be said, for at that time the Typikon commands the Priest to pronounce the verses, and not to add the Prayers besides.

3. **Entrance into the Church.** The Entrance of the Procession into the church is made in the reverse order from that in which it went out from the church, that is, first the Superior enters, then the other Priests and sacred ministers, and the entire Clergy, then the Chanters, the Brotherhood, the banner-bearers and icon-bearers, the cross-bearer, and all the people. And the Priests indeed enter into the Sanctuary and approach the Holy Table, while the Hierarch, if there be one, ascends his Throne; and the Deacon takes his stand at his place before the Royal Doors, that he may sing the Ektenia from there.

4. After the entrance into the church, the first Deacon says the Great Ektenia **"In peace let us pray to the Lord"** (*Ми́ромъ Го́споду помоли́мся*), standing at the accustomed place, and immediately we sing the Canon.

5. **The Paschal Canon:** Heirmoi 4 times (in the Greek 2 times), and Troparia for 12. (Today Heirmoi once, and Troparia with the Heirmos for 4). Katavasia after each Ode, the Heirmos of the Canon, by both Choirs together

---

[Leaf p466 / Page 464]

once. The Priest sings the Heirmoi, and the Choirs sing the Troparia and Katavasia. Refrain to the Troparia of the Canon: **"Christ is risen from the dead"** (*Христо́съ воскре́се и҆зъ ме́ртвыхъ*); at the penultimate, **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), and at the last, **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), according to custom.

At the beginning of the Canon, after the singing of the Heirmos, the Priest censes all things according to custom.[^624]

The Little Ektenia after each Ode is said by the Deacons standing at their accustomed place before the Royal Doors, with their proper Exclamations sung in turn by the Priests in the holy Sanctuary.[^625]

After the 3rd Ode, the Hypakoe; after the 6th, the Kontakion and Ikos, and **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во ви́дѣвше*) thrice, and **"Jesus is risen from the tomb"** (*Воскре́съ І҆исꙋ́съ ѿ гро́ба*) once (according to others, thrice); at the 9th Ode, at **"The Theotokos and Mother of Light"** (*Богоро́дицу и҆ Ма́терь Свѣ́та*) the customary censing takes place, and instead of **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*) we sing **"The Angel cried"** (*А҆́нгелъ вопїя́ше*) and **"Shine, shine"** (*Свѣти́ся, свѣти́ся*); after the 9th Ode, the Exaposteilarion of Pascha thrice.

6. **At the Praises**, 8 Stichera: 4 Resurrectional of the Octoechos, Tone 1, with the customary refrains from the Praises, and 4 of Pascha, with their proper refrains; then **"Glory... Both now..."** of Pascha, and **"Christ is risen"** thrice, then many times until the kiss is completed.

---

[Leaf p467 / Page 465]

7. **The Kiss of Peace.** This in the Typika is appointed at **"Christ is risen"** at the conclusion of the last Sticheron of Pascha; nevertheless, today we do not kiss one another, as the Sticheron has it, saying: **"and let us embrace one another"**, but only the Venerable Cross, the Gospel, and the Holy Icons held by the Priests, who greet each of those approaching with the words: **"Christ is risen"**, and receive the response: **"Truly He is risen"**. Furthermore, we begin the kiss not after the Paschal Stichera, but at their beginning at the Verse **"Let God arise"**, because of the many people approaching for the kiss. When very many approach, the kiss takes place even during the Canon. And this kiss according to our custom takes place thus: if there be only one Priest, he, standing in the Royal Doors, gives the Cross from there to the people to kiss, saying to each: **"Christ is risen"**, and the one kissing answers: **"Truly He is risen"**. If there be more Priests, first the Superior, having gone out with the Cross in his hand from the Royal Doors, stands before the Iconostasis on the right side, that is, by the Icon of the Savior, looking toward the north; and the second Priest, having gone out after him from the Royal Doors with the Gospel, approaches him, and the Superior gives him the Cross to kiss, saying: **"Christ is risen"**, and he having kissed it gives him the Gospel to kiss, answering: **"Truly He is risen"**, and takes his stand at his left hand; then the third Priest, having gone out with the Icon of the Resurrection of Christ, approaches the first, who gives him the Cross to kiss, saying: **"Christ is risen"**, and he having kissed it gives him the Icon of the Resurrection to kiss, answering: **"Truly He is risen"**; and he approaches the second Priest, who gives him the Gospel to kiss, saying: **"Christ is risen"**, and he having kissed the Gospel gives him the Icon of the Resurrection to kiss, answering: **"Truly He is risen"**, and

---

[Leaf p468 / Page 466]

takes his stand at the left hand of the second. And the fourth Priest, having gone out with the Icon of the Theotokos, approaches the first, then the second and the third, each of whom gives him his sacred object to kiss, saying: **"Christ is risen"**, and he having kissed it gives each of them the Icon of the Theotokos to kiss, answering: **"Truly He is risen"**; and in this manner do also the other Priests, as many as there be. In Cathedral Churches the Hierarch, sitting upon his Throne by the Icon of the Savior, gives the Cross to kiss, and likewise the Choir-clerics, each giving his sacred image to kiss, sitting upon the benches. When the kiss has been completed among the Priests, then the other sacred ministers and all the people approach one by one to each Priest according to rank, beginning from the first, and kiss his sacred emblem, answering: **"Truly He is risen"**.[^626] After the kiss there was sometimes read the Catechetical Homily of Chrysostom, which is in the Flowery Triodion.

---

[Leaf p469 / Page 467]

8. **Ektenias:** **"Have mercy on us, O God"** (*Поми́луй на́съ, Бо́же*) and **"Let us complete"** (*И҆спо́лнимъ*), by the Deacons standing at the accustomed place.

9. **Great Dismissal**, proper, at which in place of **"More honorable"** we say **"Shine, shine"**, and in place of **"Glory... Both now..."** we say **"Christ is risen"** once. The Priest having taken his stand with the Cross in the Holy Doors, the Deacon (if there be none, the Priest himself) says: **"Wisdom!"** Choir (or second Deacon, if there be one):[^627] **"Bless!"**

Priest: **"He Who is blessed and most glorified, Christ our God, always, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages."**

Choir: **"Amen. Confirm, O God, the Catholic faith, unto the ages of ages."**

Priest: **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us!"**

Choir: **"Shine, shine, O New Jerusalem... at the resurrection of thy Son."**

Priest: **"Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee!"**

Choir: **"Christ is risen from the dead... bestowing life. Lord, have mercy"** (thrice), **"Lord, bless!"**

Priest: Dismissal with the Cross: **"May Christ, Who is risen from the dead, trampling down death by death, and upon those in the tombs bestowing life, our true God, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, of the holy, glorious, and all-praised Apostles, of our venerable and God-bearing Fathers, and of all the Saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and the Lover of mankind."**

Then elevating the Cross, he says: **"Christ is risen!"** thrice, and we each time answer: **"Truly

---

[Leaf p470 / Page 468]

**He is risen!"** Then we sing the final **"Christ is risen"** thrice, the entire Troparion, and after it we conclude by chanting: **"And unto us He hath granted eternal life: we worship His three-day resurrection."**[^628]

### Note Concerning the Doors of the Iconostasis
"Be it known also this, that the Doors of the Royal Altar, both the great ones and the small ones at the sides, throughout all the churches during all of Bright Week we do not close, even at the time of Communion" (*Typikon of our Pochaiv Triodion* and *Russian Typika*).

## Paschal Hours
For each of the four Hours, likewise also for Compline and the Midnight Office, throughout all of Bright Week we say the brief Office set down in the Triodion, and in our Horologia and Prayer Books at Paschal Matins.

*Note.* If the Hours are read together, then we say **"Blessed is our God"** only at the first, while the rest we begin from **"Christ is risen"** thrice.

## At the Divine Liturgy
All things according to the general Typikon of a Feast of the Lord; only:

1. In place of **"O Heavenly King"** at the Proskomide and at the Liturgy, and wherever it may occur, we say **"Christ is risen"** thrice, even unto the Ascension; while from the Ascension unto the

---

[Leaf p471 / Page 469]

Descent [of the Holy Spirit], in place of **"O Heavenly King"** we say nothing.[^629]

2. Concerning **"Christ is risen"** it should be known that after **"Glory to Thee, O Christ God"**, before the Dismissal of the Proskomide and Liturgy, in place of **"Glory... Both now..."**, we say **"Christ is risen"** once, **"Lord, have mercy"** thrice, and **"Lord, bless"**.

After **"Blessed is the Kingdom"** we sing **"Christ is risen"** thrice; that is, the Priest once, and both Choirs once each; (although our Triodion says: the Priest thrice, and the Choirs the same thrice each); and where there is only one Choir, the Priest once and the Choir once, then half by the Priest, and half (from **"and upon those in the tombs"**) by the Choir.

Likewise also after **"With fear of God"**, in place of **"Blessed is He that cometh"**, and in place of **"We have seen the true Light"**, **"Christ is risen"** once; while in place of **"Let our mouths be filled"** and **"Blessed be the name of the Lord"**, **"Christ is risen"** thrice.[^630] Our people usually say **"Christ

---

[Leaf p472 / Page 470]

is risen"** also in place of **"Be Thou exalted above the heavens, O God"**; nevertheless, this impairs the memorial of the Mystery of Christ's Ascension, which was originally instituted at this place of the Liturgy. Our Priests also say **"Christ is risen"** (only these two words) after **"With fear of God"**, and after **"Save, O God"**, and after **"Always, now and forever"**; nevertheless, in no Typikon do we find this.

3. In place of the Trisagion we sing **"All who have been baptized into Christ"** (*Є҆ли́цы во Хрїста̀ крести́стеся*).

4. At the Reading of the Gospel, after each verse they strike all the bells.[^631]

"If the Liturgy is celebrated concelebratedly" (say our Sluzhebnyks), "then this Gospel is read by all the Priests and Deacons by verses, as the Superior shall arrange." And concerning this we have a detailed Typikon in our Triodia and the Russian ones. Nevertheless, to read one and the same Gospel by all the Priests and Deacons is a superfluous invention of the Graeco-Slavs, which today among us has a place only when the Gospel is to be

---

[Leaf p473 / Page 471]

read in various languages, as takes place in our Cathedral Churches, wherein the Hierarch reads the same in the Greek tongue from the Holy Doors, then the Deacon in Slavonic from the Ambo, and at the end the Choir-clerics and Priests in various liturgical languages, positioned throughout the church. In Russia the Hierarch reads in Slavonic, the other Priests in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin, in which the Title of the Cross was written, and then in other modern languages (Muralt, *Epistle 14*, p. 142). The Greeks likewise read the Gospel according to modern custom in various languages, yet not at the Liturgy, but at Vespers (the Gospel which is read at Vespers of this day), as takes place in the Patriarchate of Constantinople.[^632]

5. In place of **"It is truly right"**, according to the new Typikon we sing the Heirmos **"Shine, shine"**, with the refrain **"The Angel cried"**, as the Triodion and Constantinople Typikon have it, and not also with the Troparia of the 9th Ode of the Canon, as our Sluzhebnyks have, because these Troparia are not concerning the Most Holy Theotokos, but concerning Christ's Resurrection.

6. [7 in original] Before the Dismissal, in place of **"More honorable"** we say **"Shine, shine"**, and in place of **"Glory... Both now..."**: **"Christ is risen"** once; the Dismissal itself with the Cross, and the rest that follow after the Dismissal with the elevation of the Cross, without change as indicated at Paschal Matins.

7. **Blessing of the Artos.** After the Ambo Prayer[^633] takes place the blessing of the Artos, for which thou hast a prayer in the Sluzhebnik after the Liturgy of Pascha; and at the end of the prayer, the sprinkling of the Artos with holy water. And this

---

[Leaf p474 / Page 472]

Artos with the Feast, that is, with the Icon of the Resurrection, after the Dismissal of the Liturgy is carried out from the Sanctuary where it was blessed onto the Tetrapod, where it remains even unto Bright Saturday, and is kissed by the faithful entering the church. On Bright Saturday at the Liturgy after the Ambo Prayer, the Priest having gone out from the Holy Doors reads over it the Prayer for the Breaking thereof, set down in our Sluzhebnik only in the order of Bright Saturday; and thereafter having been taken from the Tetrapod, it is broken in the Sacristy, and on the morrow, that is, on Thomas Sunday after the Ambo Prayer, it is distributed to the faithful by the Priest standing in the Holy Doors.[^634]

*Note.* Throughout all of Bright Week there is dispensation for meat.

---

[Leaf p475 / Page 473]

### Blessing of Paschal Foods
This, according to our custom and according to the Typikon of the Triodion, takes place outside the church, and that either after the conclusion of the Divine Liturgy (and then going out from the church we sing the Paschal Stichera, optionally), or after Matins, or in homes on Saturday evening. The Order of this Blessing thou hast in the Sluzhebnik, in the Trebnik, in the Triodion, and in the Prayer Book after the Paschal Hours, with the sprinkling of holy water at the end.

## On the Day of Pascha at Vespers
### At Vespers
#### Note
1. The sacred ministers, vested in all the sacred vestments of their order, stand throughout all of Vespers in the Sanctuary beside the Holy Table, going out only for the Entrance (and the Deacons also for the Ektenias) before the Holy Doors, and for the final kissing of the sacred emblems, if there be more Priests, as was appointed at Matins.[^635]
2. It is censed thrice, that is, at the customary beginning only before the Holy Table, then at **"Lord, I have cried"**, and at **"Gladsome Light"** according to custom.
3. The Entrance takes place with the Gospel which is to be read.

---

[Leaf p476 / Page 474]

#### Typikon
1. The Priest and Deacons, if there be any, vested in all the sacred vestments of their order, come before the steps of the Altar and bow deeply according to custom; and the Priest having taken the censer, with the customary prayer of blessing of incense, and censing before the Holy Table, proclaims: **"Blessed is our God"**;[^636] then having handed over the censer, and ascended the steps with the Deacons, he sings **"Christ is risen"** once, and both Choirs once each. After this the Priest says clearly **"Let God arise"** and the other Verses, with **"Glory... Both now..."**, while the Choirs sing **"Christ is risen"** once or thrice after each Verse, without change as indicated at the beginning of Matins. Finally the Priest: **"Christ is risen"** up to **"trampling down death by death"**, and the Choirs: **"and upon those in the tombs bestowing life"**, and the rest.
2. **"In peace let us pray to the Lord"** the Priest says beside the Holy Table, or the Deacon before the Iconostasis.
3. **"Lord, I have cried"** in Tone 2, with the customary censing; and the Resurrection Stichera of the Octoechos of Tone 2, set down in the Triodion; **"Glory"** of the Triodion, **"Both now"**, the 1st Theotokion (Dogmatikon) of Tone 2.
4. **Entrance with the Gospel** and customary censing at **"Gladsome Light"**; and after the Great Prokimenon, the Deacon (if there be none, the Priest himself): **"And that we may be accounted worthy..."**; Priest: **"The Reading from John..."**; Deacon: **"Let us attend!"**

---

[Leaf p477 / Page 475]

then the Priest himself reads the Gospel from the Holy Doors (from John, pericope 65, up to: "I will not believe").

5. **"Let us all say"**, **"Vouchsafe, O Lord"**, and **"Let us complete"**.

6. **At the Aposticha:** One Resurrection Sticheron of the Octoechos, set down in the Triodion; then the Paschal Stichera with their refrains and the kissing of the Cross, or also of the other sacred emblems, without change as was set down at Matins; and after the final **"Christ is risen"**, immediately the Dismissal with the Cross, and the rest without change as set down at Matins.

### Compline and Midnight Office
All things according to the pattern of the Paschal Hours, here on page 468.

## General Typikon for All Days of Bright Week
### At Vespers
All things as on the day of Pascha at evening, here on page 473, except for the Entrance, which takes place with the Censer and not with the Gospel, and there is no Gospel.

#### Note
According to the earlier Typikon, the Priest at Vespers of Bright Week, from Monday onward, is not to use all the sacred vestments, but from the beginning only the epitrachelion, and from the Entrance onward also the phelonion.[^637]

---

[Leaf p478 / Page 476]

Among us the custom holds to use all the sacred vestments during the first three days of this Week, that is, on Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday evening, because our people celebrate these three days by abstaining from labor and by attending divine services. On the other days of this Week it suffices to use only the epitrachelion and phelonion.

### Compline and Midnight Office
According to the pattern of the Paschal Hours, here on page 473.

### At Matins
All things according to the Typikon of Pascha, here on page 460; only:
1. For its beginning we do not go out before the church doors, but begin it in the Sanctuary, censing before the Holy Table.[^638]
2. We say the Little Ektenia only after the 3rd, 6th, and 9th Odes.

### At the Hours
Without change as on the day of Pascha; only on Bright Saturday the 9th Hour is already said with three Psalms according to custom, and at it the Resurrection Troparion, Tone 8: **"From on high"** (*Съ высоты̀*); and the Kontakion of Pascha: **"Though Thou didst descend into the grave"** (*А҆́ще и҆ во гро́бъ*).

### At the Divine Liturgy
1. All things as on the day of Pascha, changing daily the Prokimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel.

---

[Leaf p479 / Page 477]

2. On Saturday after the Ambo Prayer we read the prayer for the breaking of the Artos, set down in our Sluzhebnik in the order of Bright Saturday.[^639]

## General Typika from Thomas Sunday unto the Ascension
The divine services from Thomas Sunday even unto the Ascension could be compressed into a general Rule within a Feast of the Lord. But since each Sunday, beginning from Thomas Sunday, has a distinct Title and a distinct Office extending to the other weekdays of the same week, and is as it were another Feast within the Feast of Pascha, for this reason in place of the Paschal Office there enters the Office of the Sunday, likewise also on weekdays, together with certain parts of the Resurrection Office of the Octoechos, except for the eight-day Feast of Mid-Pentecost, to which on weekdays the Sunday Office yields. The general rules of this time are the following:

1. At the beginning of every office, in place of **"O Heavenly King"** we sing **"Christ is risen"** thrice;[^640] and at the conclusion of every divine service, according to our custom, **"Christ is risen"** thrice; then at the conclusion we add: **"And unto us

---

[Leaf p480 / Page 478]

**He hath granted eternal life: we worship His three-day resurrection"**;[^641] and before the Dismissal, in place of **"More honorable"** we sing **"Shine, shine"**.[^642]

2. **At Vespers:** On Sunday evening for Monday an Entrance does not take place, as takes place on the Sundays of Great Lent (for here there is no Great Prokimenon, and the Triodia appoint the Ektenia **"Have mercy on us, O God"** at the conclusion of Vespers), except on Thomas Sunday, which, as a Feast of the Lord, has also a Great Prokimenon. For the rest, in the provinces on all Sunday evenings they make the Entrance even without a Feast.

3. **At Compline:** From this day we begin to sing the Canons to the Theotokos. After **"It is truly right"** we say throughout the whole week the Kontakion of the Sunday; only during the octave of the Feast of Mid-Pentecost, the Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost.

4. **The Midnight Office** we sing according to custom; only after the 1st Trisagion on the Feast of Mid-Pentecost we say the Troparion of Mid-Pentecost, and at the Apodosis of Pascha the Sunday Resurrection Troparion with its Theotokion; and after the 2nd Trisagion within Mid-Pentecost we say the Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost, but outside Mid-Pentecost the Kontakion of Pascha; while the prayers **"Remember, O Lord"** we do not say.

5. **Matins** we begin from **"Glory to the holy..."**, and immediately **"Christ is risen"** thrice, then **"Glory to God in the highest"**, and the rest; and before Psalm 50 we say **"Having beheld the Resurrection"**\n

<!-- END COHORT 1899_dolnytsky_typikon_cohort24 -->

---

<!-- START COHORT 1899_dolnytsky_typikon_cohort25 -->

[Leaf p481 / Page 479]

Christ", on Sundays indeed thrice, but on Weekdays once.[^643]

6. **At the Hours:** after **"Blessed is our God"** (*Благослове́нъ Бо́гъ на́шъ*), we say **"Christ is risen"** (*Христо́съ воскре́се*) thrice; and after the Dismissal, **"Christ is risen"** thrice, with the addition: **"And unto us He hath granted eternal life"**, and the rest.

*Note.* Since we do not say **"Blessed is our God"** when we join an Hour with Matins, or with the preceding [Hour], and likewise since we do not say the Dismissal when we join an Hour with the following [Hour], on this account neither do we say **"Christ is risen"** at that time.

7. **At the Liturgy:** we say **"Christ is risen"** in the same places as on the Resurrection of Christ, here on pages 468, 469.

The first two Antiphons are Resurrectional, but the third is the weekday one with the Resurrectional Refrain; likewise also at **"Come, let us worship"** (*Прїидѣ́те поклони́мся*), both on Sundays and on weekdays.

We conclude the Troparia with the Kontakion of Pascha,[^644] except in Thomas Week and [during the Mid-Feast of] Pentecost, for then we conclude them with their Kontakion, as the Triodion has it; although in Thomas Week also the Troparia may be concluded with the Kontakion of Pascha, as our Sluzhebnyks, and our manuscript Typikon, and the *Tserkovne Oko* do.

In place of **"It is truly meet"** (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), we sing **"The Angel cried"** (*А҆́нгелъ вопїя́ше*) and **"Shine, shine"** (*Свѣти́ся, свѣти́ся*), except during the Octave of the Mid-Feast, which has its own Heirmos.

We say the Dismissal of Pascha, except in Thomas Week, which has its own Dismissal. And we say the Dismissal with

---

[Leaf p482 / Page 480]

the Cross only on Sundays,[^645] and on the Feast of the Mid-Feast,[^646] and at the Apodosis of Pascha.[^647] We deem that on certain other days also, when there is a sufficient number of people, it will be well to say the Dismissal with the Cross, yet not on all days, as some do, having for this neither Typikon nor general custom.

8. The Service of a saint without Polyeleos occurring on these Sundays, and the rest even unto Pentecost, and on the Feast of the Mid-Feast, and at the Apodosis of Pascha, we sing at Compline.

## Proper Typika
### From Thomas Sunday to the Ascension

### Thomas Sunday
**2nd from Pascha. Tone 1.**

We celebrate an All-Night Vigil.

We sing all things according to the General Typikon of a First-Class Feast of the Lord, yet at Great Vespers without Readings, and with **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во*) thrice (according to others, once) at Matins, and without proper Antiphons at the Liturgy; and the Feast has its Apodosis on the following Saturday.

#### Weekdays of Thomas Week

On weekdays even unto the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers, we sing all things according to the General Typikon inside the Feast

---

[Leaf p483 / Page 481]

of the Feast; only at the Aposticha of Vespers, and at the Sessional Hymns of Matins which follow the 1st Kathisma-reading, and at the Praises (for there are Stichera both at the Praises and afterwards at the Aposticha) there are certain Stichera, taken from the Weekday Service of the Octoechos, according to the Tone and day of the week, except on Saturday, which has the entire Service festal. Likewise at Matins before Psalm 50 we say **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во*) once. And on Saturday we sing 3 Canons: of the Feast with the Heirmoi for 6, and of the Saint to whom the Temple is dedicated for 4, and of the Menaion for 4.

### Sunday of the Myrrh-Bearers
**3rd from Pascha. Tone 2.**

#### At Great Vespers

1. **"Blessed is our God"** (*Благослове́нъ Бо́гъ на́шъ*); **"Christ is risen"** (*Христо́съ воскре́се*) thrice; Trisagion and the rest with the **"Our Father"** (*О҆́тче на́шъ*); **"Lord, have mercy"** (*Го́споди поми́луй*) 12; **"Come, let us worship"** (*Прїидѣ́те поклони́мся*) thrice.
2. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Го́споди воззва́хъ*), 10 Stichera: 4 Resurrectional, and 6 of the Myrrh-bearers (3 from **"Lord, I have cried"**, and 3 from the Litiya); **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) of the Myrrh-bearers; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), the 1st Theotokion of the Tone (Dogmatikon).
3. At the Aposticha, the Stichera of Pascha, with their refrains; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): **"Thou Who clothest Thyself"** (*Тебѐ ѡ҆дѣ́ющагося*); **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): **"This is the day of Resurrection"** (*Воскресе́нїя де́нь*).[^648]
4. After the final Trisagion: Resurrectional Troparion, Tone 2; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный І҆ѡ́сифъ*); **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): of the Myrrh-bearers.
5. Dismissal of Pascha, without the Cross.

---

[Leaf p484 / Page 482]

#### At Compline

After **"It is truly meet"** (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), Kontakion of the Myrrh-bearers.

#### At Great Matins

1. At **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*): Resurrectional Troparion twice; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*); **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): of the Myrrh-bearers.
2. After the 1st and 2nd Kathisma-readings, Sessional Hymns of the Myrrh-bearers; and after the Evlogitaria (*Neporóchny*), **"The Angelic Host"** (*А҆́нгельскїй Собо́ръ*), and the Hypakoe of the Tone, and all the rest even unto the Canon is Resurrectional according to custom; the Resurrectional Gospel is the 2nd, and **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во*) thrice (according to others, once).
3. 3 Canons for 14: of Pascha with the Heirmos for 4, and of the Theotokos in the Triodion for 2, and of the Myrrh-bearers for 8. Katavasia of Pascha.

After the 3rd Ode, Sessional Hymn of the Triodion;[^649] after the 6th, Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion; at the 9th, we do not sing **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*),[^650] but **"The Angel cried"** (*А҆́нгелъ вопїя́ше*) and **"Shine, shine"** (*Свѣти́ся*); after the 9th, **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (*Свѧ́тъ Госпо́дь Бо́гъ на́шъ*) thrice, and the Exaposteilarion of Pascha once; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) of the Myrrh-bearers; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), the same.

4. From the Praises even unto the end, all things according to the General Typikon of every Sunday.

#### At the Hours

At all [the Hours]: Resurrectional Troparion; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*). Kontakion of the Myrrh-bearers.

---

[Leaf p485 / Page 483]

#### At the Liturgy

1. After the Entrance: Resurrectional Troparion and **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*); **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), Kontakion of the Triodion; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), of Pascha (**"Though Thou didst descend into the tomb"** (*А҆́ще и҆ во гро́бъ*)).

### Weekdays of the Week of the Myrrh-Bearers

All things according to the General Typikon of a Saint inside a Feast; only at the Aposticha of Vespers, and at the Sessional Hymns which follow the 1st Kathisma-reading of Matins, and at the Praises (for there are Stichera both at the Praises and afterwards at the Aposticha) there are certain Stichera or Troparia, taken from the Weekday Service of the Octoechos of the Tone of the week, differing according to the difference of the days of the week, except on Saturday, which has all things festal. Specifically: at Vespers at the conclusion: Troparion: **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*); **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): to the Myrrh-bearers; and the Troparia **"The noble Joseph"** and **"When Thou didst descend"** (*Є҆гда̀ снизше́лъ є҆сѝ*) we say in the evening, alternating them daily.[^651]

#### At Compline

After the Trisagion, the one Kontakion of the Sunday: "Thus we say even unto the Sunday of All Saints" (*Triodion*).

#### At Matins

At **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*), Troparion **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*) once, and **"When Thou didst descend"** (*Є҆гда̀ снизше́лъ є҆сѝ*) once; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): to the Myrrh-bearers. But when there are two Saints with

---

[Leaf p486 / Page 484]

their own Troparia, then we deem that the Resurrectional one is to be omitted.

At the Sessional Hymns and at the Praises, there are two Troparia or two Weekday Stichera of the Octoechos of the Tone of the week, with the customary refrains; and before Psalm 50, **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во*) once; and at the conclusion of Matins, the Troparia as at **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*).

#### At the Hours

Since not a single Typikon makes this clear, on this account we deem that it is to be: at the 1st [Hour], Troparion: **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*); at the 3rd, Resurrectional, and **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; at the 6th: to the Myrrh-bearers; at the 9th: again **"The noble Joseph"**, and **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint. Kontakia: at the 1st and 6th, to the Myrrh-bearers; at the 3rd and 9th, to the Saint. If two Saints occur, then at the 3rd after **"Glory"** there is the Troparion to the first, and at the 9th to the second Saint. Likewise also the Kontakia: at the 3rd to the first, and at the 9th to the second Saint.[^652]

#### At the Liturgy

Troparia: **"The noble Joseph"** (*Благообра́зный*), and Resurrectional, and to the Myrrh-bearers; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), Kontakion to the Myrrh-bearers; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion of Pascha;[^653] or **"Glory... Both now..."**, Kontakion of the Myrrh-

---

[Leaf p487 / Page 485]

bearers, without Pascha.[^654] If the Service of a Saint is also taken, or of some of the various Petitions, then after the three Troparia of the Sunday, we take also the Troparion to the Saint, or to the Petition; then Kontakion to the Myrrh-bearers, **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), Kontakion to the Saint, or to the Petition; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion of Pascha; or **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), Kontakion to the Saint, or to the Petition, and **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion to the Myrrh-bearers. Epistle and Gospel of the day; and all the rest of the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers, or also of the Saint, or of the Petition, if there be one.

### Sunday of the Paralytic
**4th from Pascha. Tone 3.**

#### At Great Vespers

1. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Го́споди воззва́хъ*), Stichera for 10: 6 of the Octoechos (set down also in the Triodion), and 4 of the Triodion; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) of the Triodion; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Dogmatikon of the Tone.
2. At the Aposticha, one Resurrectional Sticheron, then the Stichera of Pascha; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) of the Paralytic; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): **"This is the day of Resurrection"** (*Воскресе́нїя де́нь*).
3. After **"Now lettest Thou"** (*Ны́нѣ ѿпꙋща́еши*): Resurrectional Troparion, Tone 3; **"Glory... Both now..."** (*Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ*): Resurrectional Theotokion according to the Tone of the Troparion.
4. Dismissal of Pascha, without the Cross.

#### At Compline

After **"It is truly meet"** (*Досто́йно є҆́сть*), the one Kontakion of the Paralytic.

---

[Leaf p488 / Page 486]

#### At Great Matins

1. At **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*): Resurrectional Troparion twice; **"Glory... Both now..."** (*Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ*): Resurrectional Theotokion according to the Tone of the Troparion.
2. Two customary Kathismas, and Resurrectional Sessional Hymns, and the Evlogitaria (*Neporóchny*), and all the rest Resurrectional according to custom even unto the Canon, only the Resurrectional Gospel is the 4th, and **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во*) thrice.
3. 3 Canons for 14: of Pascha with the Heirmos for 6, and of the Theotokos in the Triodion for 2, and of the Paralytic for 6. Katavasia of Pascha.

After the 3rd Ode, Sessional Hymn of the Paralytic; after the 6th, Kontakion and Ikos of the Paralytic; at the 9th, we do not sing **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*), but **"The Angel cried"** (*А҆́нгелъ вопїя́ше*) and **"Shine, shine"** (*Свѣти́ся*); after the 9th, **"Holy is the Lord our God"** (*Свѧ́тъ Госпо́дь Бо́гъ на́шъ*) thrice; and the Exaposteilarion of Pascha once; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) of the Paralytic; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), the same.

4. At the Praises, 8 Resurrectional Stichera, according to custom; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) of the Paralytic; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Преблагослове́нна є҆сѝ*).
5. After the Great Doxology, one of the two Resurrectional Troparia.
6. Dismissal of Pascha; and after the Dismissal, the 4th Gospel Sticheron.

#### At the Hours

At all [the Hours]: Resurrectional Troparion, and Kontakion of the Paralytic.

#### At the Liturgy

After the Entrance: Resurrectional Troparion; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), Kontakion of the Paralytic; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion of Pascha. All the rest of the Paralytic. Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ"** (*Тѣ́ло Христо́во*) and **"Praise the Lord"** (*Хвали́те Го́спода*).

### Weekdays of the Week of the Paralytic

The Order of the Paralytic embraces only two weekdays, Monday and Tuesday, for

---

[Leaf p489 / Page 487]

on Wednesday begins already the Feast of the Mid-Feast of Pentecost.

On these two weekdays we sing all things according to the Typikon of the weekdays of the Week of the Myrrh-bearers, here on page 483; only the Troparia are thus: at the conclusion of Vespers and Matins: Resurrectional Troparion; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): Resurrectional Theotokion according to the Tone of the Troparion of the Saint.[^655] At **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*): Resurrectional Troparion twice; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): Resurrectional Theotokion according to the Tone of the Troparion of the Saint.

At all the Hours: Resurrectional Troparion, then **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*) at the 3rd and at the 9th also to the Saint; Kontakia: at the 1st and 6th, to the Paralytic; at the 3rd and 9th, to the Saint.

At the Liturgy: Resurrectional Troparion; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*), Kontakion of the Paralytic; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion of Pascha. Epistle and Gospel of the day; all the rest of the Sunday. When the Service of a Saint is also taken, or of a Petition, then: Resurrectional Troparion, and of the Saint, or of the Petition; then Kontakion of the Paralytic; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): of the Saint, or of the Petition; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion of Pascha. All the rest as above, then to the Saint, or to the Petition; only Communion Hymn: **"Receive the Body of Christ"** (*Тѣ́ло Христо́во*), and to the Saint, or to the Petition.

*Note.* If two Saints occur, it is evident that at Vespers and Matins we select the Theotokion for the Troparia according to the Tone of the second, and at **"The Lord is God"** we sing all the Troparia once.

## On Wednesday of the 4th Week from Pascha
### The Mid-Feast of Pentecost

*Note.* This Feast is a Feast of the Lord, eight-day [an Octave], beginning with the Wednesday of the Paralytic, and ending with the Wednesday of the Samaritan Woman, on which it also has its Apodosis. On the Feast itself, and at the Apodosis, the Service of the Feast

---

[Leaf p490 / Page 488]

alone is sung, while the Service of the Saint of the day from the Menaion is sung at Compline; but on the other days it is combined with the Menaion, except on the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman, for then it is combined with the Service of the Sunday. This Feast does not have an All-Night Vigil, nor a Polyeleos at Matins, but only the Great Doxology; while at Vespers there are both Entrance and Readings. We begin its Service from Tuesday evening, for the Church day begins from the evening of the preceding day.

#### Order of the Feast
##### [At Vespers]

1. The Kathisma of the day.
2. At **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Го́споди воззва́хъ*), Stichera of the Feast for 6.
3. After the Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 Readings of the Feast.
4. Aposticha of the Feast, and Troparion of the Feast, and the Great Paschal Dismissal.

##### At Compline

We sing the Stichera and Canon of the Saint of the day, and after the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Feast.

##### At Midnight Office

After the 1st Trisagion, Troparion of the Feast; and after the 2nd, Kontakion of the Feast; then **"Lord, have mercy"** (*Го́споди поми́луй*) 12, and the Dismissal. The prayers for the departed, **"Remember, O Lord"** (*Помянѝ Го́споди*), we do not say.

##### At Matins

1. At **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*): Troparion of the Feast twice; **"Glory... Both now..."** (*Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ*), the same.
2. Two customary Kathismas, with the Sessional Hymns of the Feast; then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Воскресе́нїе Христо́во*) once and Psalm 50, and immediately the Canon.
3. Two Canons of the Feast, for 14: the 1st with the Heirmos for 8, and the 2nd for 6. Katavasia: the Heirmos of the 2nd Canon.

---

[Leaf p491 / Page 489]

After the 3rd Ode, Sessional Hymn; after the 6th, Kontakion and Ikos; after the 9th, Exaposteilarion of the Feast; at the 9th, in place of **"More honorable"** (*Честнѣ́йшꙋю*), we sing the Heirmos of the Feast.

4. At the Praises, Stichera of the Feast for 4; and after the Great Doxology, Troparion of the Feast, and the Great Paschal Dismissal.

##### At the Hours

At all [the Hours], Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.

##### At the Liturgy

All things of the Feast; only the first two Antiphons are Resurrectional, and the third is the customary one with the Resurrectional Refrain; likewise also at **"Come, let us worship"** (*Прїидѣ́те поклони́мся*). In place of **"The Angel cried"** (*А҆́нгелъ вопїя́ше*) and **"Shine, shine"** (*Свѣти́ся*), we sing the Heirmos of the Feast.

### Inside the Feast of the Mid-Feast of Pentecost
*(Except the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman and the Apodosis)*

We sing all things according to the Typikon of the Feast of Thomas Sunday, here on page 477; specifically, we say the Troparia thus:

1. At the conclusion of Vespers and Matins: Troparion of the Saint; **"Glory... Both now..."** (*Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ*): of the Mid-Feast.
2. At Compline, the one Kontakion of the Mid-Feast.
3. At **"The Lord is God"** (*Бо́гъ Госпо́дь*): Troparion of the Mid-Feast twice; **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; **"Both now"** (*И҆ ны́нѣ*): of the Mid-Feast.
4. At all the Hours: Troparion of the Mid-Feast, then at the 3rd and 9th, **"Glory"** (*Сла́ва*): to the Saint; Kontakia: at the 1st and 6th, of the Mid-Feast; at the 3rd and 9th, to the Saint.
5. At the Liturgy: Troparion; **"Glory... Both now..."** (*Сла́ва, и҆ ны́нѣ*), Kontakion of the Mid-Feast.
